targets.authors: Deckert J, Nothen MM, Franke P, Delmo C, Fritze J, Knapp M et al
targets.title: Systematic mutation screening and association study of the A1 and A2a adenosine receptor genes in panic disorder suggest a contribution of the A2a gene to the development of disease.
targets.evidence_quote: Previous work has shown that a silent coding polymorphism (1083C/T, or SNP-4 in this study) in exon 2 in ADORA2A is associated with PD (Deckert et al, 1998). A Japanese group tried to replicate this finding in 87 PD patients, but found no association (Yamada et al, 2001). Given the possible importance of adenosine receptor function in panic, we proposed to study the role of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in or near the ADORA2A gene in a population of patients with PD.
targets.outcome_quote: Our findings provide evidence for a susceptibility locus for panic disorder, and possibly including agoraphobia, either within the ADORA2A gene or in a nearby region of chromosome 22, and serves as the first successful candidate gene replication study in panic disorder.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The explicit overall successful replication verdict controls despite absent single-marker association and differences in allele results.

reasoning: Title and all authors match. New family sample retests the Deckert association finding through linkage and association. Yamada is an earlier failed replication discussed as background, not the finding retested. Other prior genetic and phenotype studies provide context or data methods.
